item.title: A Captive Teen Helped Police Catch John Jamelske
item.description: In 2003, a 16-year-old held captive by John Jamelske called her sister during an errand, helping police uncover kidnappings spanning 15 years. He pleaded guilty to five kidnapping counts and was sentenced to 18 years to life. Individual victims were held for months or years.

item.title: Five Women Testified That Phil Spector Threatened Them With Guns
item.description: At Phil Spector’s murder trial, five women described earlier incidents in which he threatened them with guns. The music producer was convicted of murdering actress Lana Clarkson in 2009 and sentenced to 19 years to life in prison.

item.title: Why Austin Harrouff Was Sent To A Hospital After Killing Two
item.description: Austin Harrouff was 19 when he killed John Stevens III and Michelle Mishcon at their Florida home in 2016. After experts concluded he suffered an acute psychotic episode, a judge found him not guilty by reason of insanity in 2022 and ordered him committed to a secure mental health facility.

item.title: The Diary Entry Alyssa Bustamante Tried To Erase
item.description: After 15-year-old Alyssa Bustamante killed nine-year-old Elizabeth Olten in Missouri in 2009, she obscured a diary entry describing the murder. A forensic examiner recovered the text using ultraviolet light. She pleaded guilty in 2012 and received life with parole eligibility, plus 30 years.

item.title: Christa Pike Told Classmates She Had Killed Colleen Slemmer
item.description: In 1995, 18-year-old Christa Pike helped lure fellow Job Corps student Colleen Slemmer away from their Knoxville campus, then told classmates she had killed her. Prosecutors said Pike viewed Slemmer as a romantic rival. Pike was convicted of murder and sentenced to death.

item.title: Clavicular’s Livestream Became Evidence In A Rape Investigation
item.description: Looksmaxxing influencer Braden Peters, known as Clavicular, faces charges over an alleged 2025 assault on a 17-year-old in Massachusetts. Police reviewed livestream footage as part of the investigation. He pleaded not guilty in October 2026 and was released on $10,000 bail.

item.title: Sheila Davalloo Disguised An Attempted Murder As A Game
item.description: In 2003, Sheila Davalloo persuaded her husband to play a blindfolded guessing game, then stabbed him. He survived and later testified at her trial for Anna Lisa Raymundo’s murder. Davalloo received consecutive sentences of 25 years for attempted murder and 50 years for murder.

item.title: Shelly Knotek’s Daughters Exposed The Deaths Inside Her Home
item.description: In 2003, Shelly Knotek’s daughters told police about abuse inside their Washington home. Investigators found Ronald Woodworth buried in the backyard. Knotek entered Alford pleas to murder and manslaughter in the deaths of Kathy Loreno and Woodworth, receiving more than 22 years in prison.
